text.flavor: While the road waits, the Host takes up the work at hand: hauling, mending, tending, building, and drilling for what comes next.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Gain 2 Coin.
  • Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership.
  • Repair Baggage: Spend 1 Wood to repair 1 damaged Baggage Train space.

If you have Camp Steward: After resolving Work, you may search the surrounding area for opportunities. Roll 1d6:
  • 1–4, A Willing Trader: Buy 1 Resource for 1 Coin less than Market Buy (minimum 1 Coin), or sell 1 Resource at Market Sell value.
  • 5–6, A Fortunate Discovery: Gain 1 Resource matching adjacent Terrain for free.
You may purge Baggage contents to make room for a new Resource.

text.flavor: Travelers, merchants, and wanderers gather around the Host's fires. Some bring gifts, others bring stories, and a few bring troubles not yet known.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time.

Gain 2 Coin and 1 Leadership.

Add 1 random Scene from the unseeded Scene deck to the Camp discard pile.

After play: Choose to Remove or Discard this card.

text.flavor: Stone and timber raise the walls, but belief and learning decide what kind of place stands within them.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Chapel: Cost: 1 Wood and 1 Coin. Gain Priest.
  • Academy: Cost: 1 Stone and 1 Coin

Place the matching token on your Player Board.

text.flavor: The frontier yields little to those who only pass through. It rewards the ones who leave something behind.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Market: Cost: 1 Wood and 1 Coin.
  • Baggage Cart: Cost: 1 Wood

Place the matching token on your Player Board.

text.flavor: Silver spent on quiet study often returns in louder ways.
text.effect: Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Coin and Gain 1 Research token.

text.flavor: There are always swords for hire where fear is near and silver is honest.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time Recruit up to 2 Mercenaries (Infantry class) for 1 Coin each.

Mercenaries:
  • May exceed Host MU limits
  • Use white Mercenary tokens.

Reminder: Mercenaries disband in Winter.

text.flavor: A shared meal and a welcoming fire restore the Host's spirits. The locals offer what their land provides.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time. Spend 1 Food.

Choose 2 different options:
  • Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Gain 1 Morale.
  • Gain 1 Resource matching the adjacent Terrain, subject to Baggage Train capacity.

text.flavor: The march pauses long enough for weariness to loosen its grip.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Leadership.

Gain 2 Leadership and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Not every man who joins the host seeks glory. Some answer because the road has reached their door.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:

Raise Levies: Spend 1 Food. Add 2 Levy to your Host.

- or -
Rest: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A host that trains in earnest soon learns what kind of war it means to fight.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Leadership.

Choose 1:
  • You may immediately purchase either the top card of the Advancement deck or 1 Armor Development from the R&R Offer. It costs 1 less Research Token, to a minimum of 1. You must still pay all other printed costs.
  • Gain 1 Research. You may discard the top Advancement card for free and reveal the next one, though you may not purchase it during this phase.


After making your choice, gain 1 Leadership

text.flavor: A gift sent ahead may cool a grudge that steel would only sharpen.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time. Choose 1 Hostile tribe. Spend one of the following as a gift to that tribe: 2 Coin, 1 Food, 1 Wood, 1 Stone, or 1 Research. Then make a 6+ test. Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM, and Leadership may not be spent on this test.

Pass: Gain 1 Rapport with that tribe and gain 1 Morale.

Fail: No effect.

text.flavor: A wise commander does not march on courage alone. Scouts find the road, and Stewards keep the Host ready to follow it.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
Train Scouts: Cost: 1 Coin. Place the Scouting token near the Explore draw deck.

Appoint Camp Steward: Cost: 2 Coin. Place the Camp Steward token near the Camp draw deck.

text.flavor: Bread shared in peace can carry a promise farther than a threat ever will.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Food.

Choose a Neutral or Friendly tribe and test 6+, applying any Rapport DRM. Leadership may not be spent on this test.

  • Pass: Gain 2 Coins and 1 Leadership, then:
    • If the tribe is Neutral, gain 1 Rapport with that tribe.
    • If the tribe is Friendly, gain 1 additional Leadership instead.
  • Fail: No effect.

text.flavor: The mugs keep coming, the dice keep rolling, and good judgment is first out the door.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. You may pay 1 coin to Roll 1d6. You may not use Leadership to alter your result:
1: Lose 1 Morale. Your host shakes their head in disapproval.
2: Leave the tavern with your reputation intact.
3: Gain 1 Coin.
4: Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.
5: Gain 2 Coins and 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.
6: Gain 3 Coins, 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.

text.flavor: A crowd of angry villagers blocks the road ahead, armed with pitchforks, cudgels, and whatever else was close at hand. They have gathered in protest against a local Lord, but their anger has spilled into the streets. Stones fly, windows shatter, and as your Host approaches, the crowd surges toward your men.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Reason with the Crowd: Test 8+.
    • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership. Seed 1 random MR Echo.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.
  • Show Force: Test 7+.
    • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Levy.
  • Hold the Line: Advance 1 Time. No further effect.

text.flavor: Before the gathered faithful, your victory was an insult that could not be ignored. The fire has not forgotten. It comes now to burn shame away in battle.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Sun-Touched are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Sun-Touched are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9+). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 2A, 2I, 1L
Year 2: 3A, 2I, 2L
Year 3: 2A, 1C, 2I, 3L

text.flavor: They do not howl for vengeance. They come in silence, pale faces streaked with ash, to reclaim what was taken and punish the hand that dared to hold it.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Pale Hands are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Pale Hands are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 3I, 2L
Year 2: 1A, 3I, 3L
Year 3: 1A, 4I, 3L

text.flavor: The Nightstone Clan does not forgive defeat. They watch, they wait, and when you grow comfortable behind your own walls, they strike with cold purpose.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Nightstone Clan are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Nightstone Clan are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 2A, 1C, 2I
Year 2: 1A, 1C, 2I, 2L
Year 3: 2A, 1C, 2I, 3L

text.flavor: No oath was shouted. No challenge was given. Yet the trespass lingers like a stain. When the Quietus comes, it does so with the certainty of a sentence already passed.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Quietus are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Quietus are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 1P, 1A, 1I, 2L
Year 2: 1P, 1A, 1I, 5L
Year 3: 1P, 1A, 2I, 6L

text.flavor: A child’s careless game has set dry kindling smoldering near a granary. The danger is small now. It will not stay that way for long.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 2d6:
8+: The fire is put out in time for grateful eyes to see it. Gain 1 Morale. Seed 1 random QS Echo.

7 or less: The flame is stamped out before anyone even notices. No effect.

text.flavor: The child’s little blaze never reached the granary, and the people nearby know why. News of your host’s quick action has traveled ahead of the march to places where full storehouses still matter.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Food, 1 Wood, and 1 Morale.

Those who heard the tale offer provisions freely, grateful that your host once kept smoke from becoming ruin.

ECHO-Q-02.title: The Child Still Tells the Story

text.flavor: The child whose game set the kindling smoking still tells how your host stepped in before the flames could spread to the granary. The tale has moved ahead of your march, and strangers now look on your host more favorably than they otherwise would.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Morale and 1 Leadership.

People receive your host more warmly, and that goodwill lends extra weight to your words.

text.flavor: The child’s little blaze that threatened the granary did not begin as carelessly as it seemed. Now, the one who meant the granary to burn finds your host and makes their displeasure known.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6:
1-2: Lose 1 Leadership. They catch your host off guard and muddy the truth before witnesses.

3-4: No effect. The accusation comes to nothing, but leaves a sour taste.

5-6: Gain 1 Leadership. Your host turns the confrontation back on them and comes away looking sharper.

text.flavor: There is shouting at Pepperridge Farm that draws your host’s attention. Dr. Pepper, known nearby for treating sick horses and troubled cattle, and his family are being harassed by the Crumb family, a local rival bakery, who accuse them of stealing recipes. The Crumbs offer food and silver for your backing, though your host can see well enough that both were taken from the Pepper family’s own stores.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. You may side with the Crumb family.

If you do, gain 2 Food and 5 Coin. Seed 1 random CR Echo. Otherwise, seed 1 random DP Echo.

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as rich as it had hoped. Dr. Pepper took solace in knowing that the food taken from his family’s stores would do your host no good. A man who knows beasts and sickness also knows what spoiled stores can do to a marching army.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6:
1–4: Lose 1 Infantry and 2 Levy. The food taken that day turned foul in camp, and the sickness that followed was no accident.
5–6: Signs of tampering are discovered in time. No units are lost.

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as unnoticed as it had hoped. The silver taken from that quarrel is long spent, but the insult has only grown in the telling.
text.effect:
Now Dr. Pepper has caught up with your march, backed by furious kin, flour-dusted bakers, and enough hard-handed farm folk to make good on his grievance at last.

Advance 1 Time and Fight a Combat against Dr. Pepper’s Host, consisting of 2A, 1C, 3I and 4L. You may not disengage from this combat. If you lose, you are defeated by Dr. Pepper. From Pepperridge Farm. Because you stuck your nose into a dispute over baked goods and your campaign ends.

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as quietly as it had hoped. Dr. Pepper has seen to it that the story spread ahead of your march, and always in the same telling: your host took stolen food and silver because greed came easier than judgment.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6:
1–5: The tale has done its work. You have been arrested and face justice from the local law.

Advance 1 Time. Lose 5 Coin and 1 Morale.

If you cannot pay the full 5 Coin, lose all Coin you have and spend the next week in the town gaol. Advance the calendar 1 additional space for time served.

The silver is seized, the fine is paid, and your host leaves with a new name in local gossip: the Baked Good Bandits.
6: Your Host evades the authorities. No effect.

text.flavor: A family’s cart has broken an axle in the mud, and much of their life lies scattered in the road around them. Others have passed them by. Your Host can stop, lend hands, and set the cart right before the road swallows the day entire.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Help the Family: Advance 1 Time and roll 2d6.
    • 6+: The cart is righted, the axle bound well enough to travel, and the family parts from your Host with gratitude plain on every face. Gain 1 Morale. Seed 1 random SC Echo.
    • 5 or less: The cart is righted all the same, but the help is taken more as necessity than kindness. No effect.
  • Pass By: Seed 1 random KB Echo.

text.flavor: The family whose cart your host helped right did not remain unlucky for long. A letter reached them not many weeks later bearing news of a previously unknown kinsman and an inheritance they had never expected to see. Remembering who stopped in the mud when others rode on, they have sought your host out to repay the kindness in full.
text.effect: Gain 1 Food, 3 Coin, and 1 Morale.

ECHO-C-02.title: The Road Was Spoken Well Of

text.flavor: The family whose cart your host helped right had no silver windfall to share, but neither did they let the kindness vanish into the mud. They spoke of your host wherever the road carried them, and the tale has gone ahead of your march in quieter ways than coin.
text.effect: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A roadside shrine has become a place of local giving. Candles burn low, coins sit in the offering bowl, and food for the poor rests under cloth beside the stone.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. When your host stops nearby, a sudden uproar breaks out: silver is missing, and one of your men is being named as the thief. The charge cannot be proven, but your host can feel how badly the locals want someone to answer for it.

You leave the matter unsettled and march on rather than lose time to finding the truth. Seed 1 random MA Echo.

text.flavor: The silver missing from the shrine was not misplaced after all. Word has caught up with your host that the accused man truly did take it, and now the locals mean to see the matter answered. The culprit is handed over to the law, and your host must make what restitution it can besides.
text.effect: Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Morale and spend 2 Coin in restitution.

text.flavor: The silver missing from the shrine was taken, but not by the man named under your banner. The true thief has been found, and the accusation that followed your host falls away at last.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Morale.

The man’s name is cleared, and the relief runs through the host faster than the rumor ever did.

text.flavor: A stranger challenges the Host to a contest of strength. A muddy ring forms at the edge of camp as coins flash and voices rise. Your men look to you. Will you name a champion to face him?
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. Choose 1:
  • Refuse the Challenge: Lose 1 Leadership.
  • Send in a Fighter: Requires at least 1 Military Unit in your Host (Levy alone do not qualify). Roll 1d6:
    • 1: Lose 1 Morale. Seed 1 random WB Echo.
    • 2–3: Seed 1 random WB Echo.
    • 4–5: Gain 2 Coin. Seed 1 random WA Echo.
    • 6: Gain 3 Coin and 1 Morale. Seed 1 random WA Echo.

text.flavor: The victory has become a campfire legend, retold louder with every passing night.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Your champion’s name travels ahead of the Host, drawing cheers, wagers, and eager hangers-on.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Leadership.

You may recruit 1 Levy for free.

text.flavor: The bruises from the wager have faded, but resentment lingers. Some among the Host question why their commander’s pride was worth a fellow soldier’s blood.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Hear Their Grievance: Advance 1 Time.
  • Dismiss Their Complaints: Lose 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: The contest is long over, but the bitterness remains. A band of angry gamblers catches up with your Host, accusing your champion of deliberately throwing the fight to profit from the wagers. They demand restitution.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Pay Them Off: Spend 2 Coin.
  • Refuse Their Demand: Test 7+. On a failure, lose 1 Morale.

SCENE-021.title: The Pig That Became a Lord

text.flavor: At a neighboring village fair, a fat prize pig escapes its pen, charges through a council moot, knocks over a local banner, and settles proudly into the Lord’s chair. The locals begin arguing whether this is an omen, a joke, or treason. You make a jape about how much the pig resembles the Lord.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Refer to your Rapport with the tribe in or closest to your Host’s location.
  • Friendly or Allied: Seed 1 random PA Echo.
  • Neutral or Hostile: Seed 1 random PB Echo.

text.flavor: Word of the jape spreads faster than your Host. By the time the tale catches up with you, the Lord himself has claimed the pig as a lucky fool and your jest as proof of good humor.
text.effect: Gain 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: Camp followers, traders, and road-wardens repeat the story with laughter rather than malice. For a few days, your Host is remembered as clever company instead of another column of armed strangers.
text.effect: Gain 1 Coin or 1 Food.

text.flavor: The tale reaches the Lord in a sharper form than you intended. Weeks later, an enormous roasted pig is delivered to your camp, accompanied by a message bearing the Lord’s seal: “His Lordship sends his regards.”
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Accept the Feast: Gain 1 Food. Lose 1 Morale.
  • Refuse the Gift: Seed 1 random RG Echo.

text.flavor: A small party of offended retainers reaches your camp carrying the insult in full ceremonial outrage. They insist the story has made their lord a laughingstock across the road.
text.effect: Lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A village keeps firepots, pitch jars, and old siege oil for defense. The stores are dangerous, poorly sealed, and exactly the sort of thing that could break an enemy line if used first.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Take the Firepots: Place the Firepots token in your Baggage Train. Seed one random FF Echo.
  • Condemn the Stockpile: Gain 1 Leadership.

Firepots effect: Before the first round of a Combat you may discard it to roll 3d6. For each 4+ rolled, assign 1 casualty to the enemy Host. Assign casualties as if it were a Cavalry attack.

text.flavor: The jars were never meant to travel. One cracks in the night, and the Baggage Train wakes to smoke, shouting, and burning straw.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. If the Firepots token remains in your Baggage Train, Test 7+ (Leadership cannot be spent on this test).
Pass: Choose 1:
  • Keep the Firepots and discard this Echo.
  • Remove the Firepots token and remove this Echo from the game.

Fail: BANG! BANG! Remove the Firepots token. Damage its Baggage Train slot and 1 adjacent Baggage Train slot of your choice. If the adjacent slot contains a Resource, lose that Resource. Remove this Echo from the game.

If you no longer have Firepots, remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The pitch seeps through its wrappings. The stink spreads through the carts, clings to blankets, fouls food, and makes every soldier nervous about striking sparks.
text.effect:
If the Firepots token is still in your Baggage Train, Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Dump the Firepots: Remove the Firepots token from your Baggage Train and Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Carry the Risk: Remove this card from the game and Seed the remaining FF Echo into the Camp discard pile.

If the Firepots token is no longer in your Baggage Train, Remove this card.

text.flavor: A battlefield surgeon offers the Host a bitter black draught used by mercenaries who need men standing longer than men should. He does not call it medicine. He calls it time bought in advance.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Take the Draught: Gain 4 Painkiller doses. Seed the PK Echo.
  • Refuse the Dose: Gain 1 Morale.


Painkiller: Whenever a Military Unit or Levy would be lost, you may spend 1 dose and roll 1d6. On 5–6, prevent that loss. On 1–4, the dose fails. You may spend another dose to attempt to prevent the same loss. Each roll consumes 1 dose.

text.flavor: The draught still works. That may be the worst thing about it.
text.effect:
If no Painkiller doses remain, remove this Echo and draw a replacement Camp card.

Otherwise, Test 8+ (Leadership may be spent).
Pass: Discard this Echo. Keep any unused Painkiller doses.
Fail: Lose 1 Morale. Remove all remaining Painkiller doses and this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The officers find a marching cadence that keeps the Host moving long after common sense says to stop. Boots strike road. Wagons creak. No one complains because no one has breath left to complain.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Force the March: Gain the Forced March token. Gain +1 Morale and 1 Leadership. Seed one random LK Echo.
  • Keep a Human Pace: No effect.

Forced March effect: While this token is active, your Explore phase costs 1 Time instead of 2 Time.

text.flavor: The rhythm is breaking. Men stumble, curses spread, and the road begins taking payment in flesh and patience.
text.effect:
Test 7+.

  • Pass: Choose 1:
    • Keep the Cadence: Lose 1 Leadership. Discard this Echo. Keep the Forced March token.
    • Call a Halt: Advance 2 Time. Remove the Forced March token. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Fail: Remove the Forced March token. Lose 1 Leadership. Remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The cadence holds. The Host moves faster than it should, farther than it wants, and harder than any road has a right to demand.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Spend Discipline: Lose 1 Leadership. Discard this Echo. Keep the Forced March token.
  • Let Them Breathe: Remove the Forced March token. Gain 1 Morale. Remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The Host tries to forget what it accepted, but the story has already learned to march.
text.effect:
If the Reign in Blood token is active, make a standard Morale test.
  • Pass: Remove the Reign in Blood token. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Fail: Discard this Echo. The Reign in Blood token remains active.

If the Reign in Blood token is not active, remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: Men who once looked away now speak more easily of what must be done. The road has taught them a lesson, and they have learned it too well.
text.effect:
If the Reign in Blood token is active, lose 1 Morale and make a standard Morale test.
Pass: Remove the Reign in Blood token and this Echo from the game.
Fail: Regain 1 Morale. Retain the Reign in Blood token; discard this Echo.

If the token is not active, remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: Word reaches the Host that the dead were found buried, named where possible, and left with enough dignity that strangers stopped to notice.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: An old seer comes to the Host, offering a glimpse of roads not yet taken and choices still within reach.
text.effect: Alter Your Fate: Look at the top 3 Camp cards. You may permanently remove 1 ordinary Camp card or Echo from the game. If it is a Hostile Echo, return it to the unseeded Echo Supply instead. Special cards cannot be removed. You may discard any number of the remaining cards and return the rest to the top in any order.

text.flavor: A broad-shouldered local called Big ’Orra strides into camp, points at your banner, and unleashes a speech no one understands. It sounds important. Possibly friendly. Possibly murderous. You answer with equivalent gibberish. This may have been unwise.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 1d6.
  1. ’Orra goes red with fury and lands a big, meaty fist in your face. Lose 1 Morale.
  2. ’Orra spits and gestures sharply. You appear to owe him something. Lose 1 Coin.
  3. No one understands anyone. No Effect.
  4. ’Orra nods as if a serious matter has been settled. Gain 1 Leadership.
  5. ’Orra roars with laughter and claps you on the shoulder. Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership.
  6. ’Orra declares you a person of rare wisdom. Apparently. Gain 2 Coin and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A local priest leads an unfamiliar rite just beyond camp. The drums, chants, and strange gestures unsettle the Host. Soon your soldiers are watching more than resting.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Let the Rite Continue: Seed 1 random RC Echo.
  • Interrupt the Priest: Advance 1 Time. Gain 1 Leadership. Seed 1 random SR Echo.
  • Let Your Priest Judge It: Requires Priest. Test 7+.
    • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Morale. Seed 1 random RC Echo.
    • Fail: Advance 1 Time. Seed 1 random SR Echo.

text.flavor: Word reaches your Host that the local priest has spoken well of your restraint. Grateful that his people were permitted to complete their sacred rite in peace, he sends a blessing for the road ahead.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A written complaint reaches camp, sealed and formal. Though the rite proceeded undisturbed, some among the faithful regarded the presence of armed strangers at their sacred ceremony as an offense in itself.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Answer the Charge: Lose 1 Leadership.
  • Make Restitution: Spend 2 Coin.
  • Let Doctrine Speak: Requires Priest. Test 7+.
    • Pass: No effect.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A violent storm breaks over the Host. By morning, locals say the sky opened because your Host disturbed what it did not understand.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time, Lose 1 Morale.

If you have a Priest, you may Test 7+.
  • Pass: Do not lose the Morale.

ECHO-H-02.title: Falling Off the Edge of the World

text.flavor: Since the rite was disturbed, the road has felt less certain. Guides contradict themselves. Landmarks seem to lose meaning. Even your camp staff begin to doubt their maps.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Stop and Regroup: Advance 1 additional Time. No further effect.
  • Press On: Test 8+ (6+ if you have Scouting).
    • Pass: No further effect.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-01.title: Sacred Heart

text.flavor: The old stones are remembered by those who still hold your Host close. What was found beneath the trees has become a sign that the road between you has not yet broken.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with the Quietus.
Allied: Gain 1 Morale or 1 Leadership.
Friendly: No effect.
Neutral or Hostile: Test 7+. On failure, lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-01.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-02.title: Believer

text.flavor: The Sabbath Stones marked more than old prayer. They marked expectation. The Quietus remember whether your Host treated that expectation as a beginning, a promise, or a thing left behind.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with the Quietus.
Allied: Gain 1 Leadership.
Friendly: No effect.
Neutral: Lose 1 Leadership.
Hostile: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-02.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-03.title: Last in Line

text.flavor: The stones offered no easy meaning when first you found them. Perhaps they were warning. Perhaps invitation. The Quietus now judge what your Host made of the space between you.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with the Quietus.
Allied: Gain 1 Morale.
Friendly: Gain 1 Leadership.
Neutral: No effect.
Hostile: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-03.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-04.title: Shot in the Dark

text.flavor: The Sabbath Stones were found while the Quietus stood against you. If there was a lesson in that ring of old marks, it was not freely given. Now the road asks whether anything changed.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with the Quietus.
Allied: Gain 2 Leadership and 2 Morale.
Friendly: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Morale.
Neutral: Gain 1 Morale.
Hostile: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-04.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

text.flavor: Tiny bootprints appear around the Baggage Train each morning. The soldiers laugh at first, blaming “fair folk with marching orders.” Then flour is spilled, straps are loosened, and someone finds a child-sized print inside a sealed cart.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Laugh It Off: Gain 1 Morale. Seed one random FB Echo.
  • Set a Watch: Gain 1 Leadership. Lose 1 Morale.
  • Let Your Priest Name It: Requirement: Priest. Test 8+.
    • Pass: Gain 1 Morale and 1 Leadership.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale. Seed one random FB Echo.

text.flavor: The watch finally catches two children slipping away from the Baggage Train with stolen provisions. They insist the food is for their friends and lead your men to a neglected burial ground. There, they lay the provisions beside several small, weathered headstones. “They still get hungry,” whispers one. As your men examine the graves, the children disappear. Their tiny footprints lead to the headstones, but none lead away.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Leave the Offerings: Lose 1 Food. Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Reclaim the Provisions: No effect.

text.flavor: The mystery ends in a sack of gnawed crusts, a nest under the cart boards, and enough droppings to make the cooks swear off breakfast.
text.effect:
If you have a Camp Steward, you may Test 6+.
Pass: No effect.
Fail: Lose half your Food, rounded up.

If you have no Camp Steward, lose half your Food, rounded up.

text.flavor: A familiar figure approaches the fire, smiling beneath a road-worn hat. Dr. Pepper has not forgotten the day your Host stood with his family. He shares your fire, offers his counsel, and before departing clasps your arm. “You stood with the Peppers when it mattered. As far as I'm concerned, that makes you one of us.”
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale and 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: The Crumbs have not forgotten your slight at Pepperridge Farm. They descend upon your camp at last, armed with pitchforks, cudgels, and a grudge they have clearly been nursing since you parted ways. It seems the Crumbs remember, too.
text.effect:
Battle 6 Levy.

Crumb Levy do not Rout when they roll a 1.

If you Disengage, the Camp phase ends.

text.flavor:
What began as kin, peddlers, runaways, failed soldiers, and other hangers-on has become something closer to a village on the march. They trail the Baggage Train, sleep beyond the fires, trade among themselves, and answer to no officer.

Most are harmless enough. Probably.

Lately, however, too many small troubles seem to begin in their part of camp.
text.effect:
Seed a random RR Echo
When resolving a Riff Raff Echo, refer to the Riff Raff Rules card.

text.flavor: The camp followers have been busy. Of course they have.
text.effect:
2-3: Jailbreak - Some camp followers help a troublesome Levy slip away before punishment can be carried out. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Levy. If you have no Levy, lose 1 Morale instead.
4-6: Problem Child - Another mess demands an officer's attention. Advance 1 Time.
7: Ride On - For once, they mind their own business. No effect.
8-10: Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap - Something unpleasant needed doing. The camp followers handled it before anyone thought to ask how. Gain 1 Coin.
11-12: Big Balls - An outrageous wager somehow pays off. Some of the winnings even reach the Host. Gain 2 Coin.

text.flavor: The Riff Raff have wandered farther than usual. That is rarely a good sign.
text.effect:
2-3: If You Want Blood (You've Got It) - A brawl turns ugly before the Host can stop it. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Morale.
4-6: Night Prowler - Someone has been prowling the camp after dark. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Coin.
7: Beating Around the Bush - Plenty of talk, little action. No effect.
8-10: Shot Down in Flames - The Riff Raff expose a petty scheme before it reaches the Host. Gain 1 Leadership.
11-12: Highway to Hell - One of the followers knows a disreputable shortcut. Place a reminder cube on the Explore deck. Your next Explore does not advance Time.

text.flavor: The camp followers have found new ways to keep themselves occupied. The Host may regret noticing.
text.effect:
2-3: Kicked in the Teeth - A quarrel with locals ends badly. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Morale.
4-6: Down Payment Blues - A creditor arrives with a bill for something bought in the Host's name. Lose 1 Coin or advance 1 Time.
7: Dog Eat Dog - They cheat, hustle, and quarrel among themselves. No effect.
8-10: Whole Lotta Rosie - Rosie's side business is thriving. The Host gets a cut. Gain 1 Coin.
11-12: The Jack - One of Rosie's customers returns with an embarrassing complaint. Soon everyone is laughing at the poor bastard. Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: While some faces have changed, the Riff Raff remain much the same. Trouble still follows.
text.effect:
2-3: Night of the Long Knives - A vicious feud erupts among the followers. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Morale.
4-6: This House Is on Fire - A cookfire spreads through the followers' tents and stores. Advance 1 Time. Lose 1 Food.
7: Fly on the Wall - Rumors pass through camp all night. None prove useful. No effect.
8-10: Thunderstruck - Lightning fells a tree near camp. The followers waste no time putting it to use. Gain 1 Wood.
11-12: Moneytalks - A few followers prove surprisingly capable fighters. You may recruit up to 2 Infantry for 1 Coin each.

text.flavor: Weeks may have passed since the toll was refused, but resentment travels roads the Host no longer walks. Word comes that old enemies have struck at the Host's holdings.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: Destroy your Market. If you do not have a Market, lose 1 Morale.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: The brigands themselves are long gone from sight. Their grudge is not. Somewhere beyond the camp, men with old directions and fresh malice set their hands to ruin.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: Destroy your Academy. If you do not have an Academy, lose 1 Morale.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: The choice was made on a distant road, and for a time it seemed forgotten. Now the debt returns, carried by fire, rumor, and men who remember being denied.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: If you have a Temple, destroy it and lose your Priest. If you do not have a Temple, lose 1 Morale.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: A delegation comes before the Host with torn cloaks, empty hands, and voices too loud to ignore. They come not with tribute, but with a plea. Their need is plain. So is the question beneath it: will the Host stand with those who once stood aside for them?
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time.

The tribe with your highest Rapport asks the Host for aid. If tied, choose one.

Choose 1:
  • Answer the Call: Spend 2 Food or 2 Coin. Gain 1 Morale.
  • Send Protection: Lose 1 Infantry or 1 Archer. Gain 1 Morale.
  • Turn Them Away: Reduce that tribe's Rapport by 1 step and seed 1 random SS Echo.

text.flavor: The story changes as it travels. By the time it reaches other fires, the Host did not lack the means to help. It lacked the will.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: Place a reminder token near the Rapport area of the Calendar. The next time you would gain Rapport with any tribe, do not gain it. Then remove the reminder token.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: A name once spoken with hope is now spoken with bitterness. Somewhere in the realm, those who expected aid have learned to expect less.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: Reduce the Rapport of the tribe with your highest Rapport by 1 step. If tied, choose one.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: The plea was left behind, but not forgotten. Around the Host's fires, the tale returns in quieter voices, and no one is comforted by the telling.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6. Leadership may not be spent.
  • 1-4: Lose 1 Morale. If any tribe is Hostile, lose 2 Morale instead.
  • 5-6: No effect.

text.flavor: The road has settled into the Host's bones. Boots split, wheels groan, and every dawn sounds less like a beginning than a sentence being carried out.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. Make a Morale test. Leadership may not be spent. Do not apply the Priest modifier.
  • Pass: No effect.
  • Fail: Place the Slow March token on or near the Explore deck and seed Echo BT1.
While the Slow March token is active, each Explore Step costs 3 Time instead of 2.

text.flavor: The slow march has not ended. Men rise late, scouts return slower, and every mile seems to take more from the Host than it should.
text.effect:
Make a Morale test. Leadership may not be spent. Do not apply the Priest modifier.
  • Pass: Remove the Slow March token. Remove this Echo. Explore Steps cost 2 Time again.
  • Fail: Discard this Echo. The Slow March token remains. Explore Steps continue to cost 3 Time.

ECHO-KB-01.title: Someone Else Stopped

text.flavor: A passing merchant eventually helped the stranded family. Word reaches your Host that they arrived home safely, their ordeal already fading into memory.
text.effect: No effect.

ECHO-KB-01.notes: Seeded by: Set the Cart Right

ECHO-KB-02.title: A Wheel of Misfortune

text.flavor: Your baggage cart strikes a deep rut, splintering its wooden sideboards. As the men survey the damage, an old soldier mutters, “As a man sows, so shall he reap.”
text.effect: Damage 1 Baggage Train slot. You may immediately spend 1 Wood and advance 1 Time to repair it. Otherwise, the slot remains damaged.

ECHO-KB-02.notes: Seeded by: Set the Cart Right

ECHO-RG-01.title: The Swine’s Toll

text.flavor: At a narrow crossing, the Lord’s tollmen wave other travelers through. When your Host approaches, they lower the barrier and produce a writ bearing his seal.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Pay the Toll: Spend 3 Coin.
  • Find Another Road: Advance 2 Time.
  • Attack the Tollmen: Lose 1 Rapport with the tribe in or closest to your Host’s location. Enter Combat against Infantry equal to Game Year + 1.

ECHO-RG-01.notes: Seeded by: A Joke Grows Teeth

ECHO-RG-02.title: The Last Word

text.flavor: A herald arrives at your camp bearing a scroll adorned with the Lord’s seal. He unfurls it with great ceremony, clears his throat, and reads: “One swine refuses another? Very well. You mistook a pig for a lord; I mistook you for a gentleman. Let us call our errors even.” He hands you the scroll, bows, and departs.
text.effect: No Effect.

ECHO-RG-02.notes: Seeded by: A Joke Grows Teeth

text.flavor: News of your Host peacefully dispersing an angry mob travels across the realm. The tale reaches a nearby Tribe, whose people speak favorably of your restraint and the bloodshed you prevented.
text.effect: Gain 1 Rapport with the tribe in or closest to your Host’s location.

text.flavor: Word reaches your Host from the village where you quelled the angry crowd. The Lord has sold the land upon which the village stands. Its new master has driven the inhabitants from their homes and fields, recognizing none of their former claims. The families now wander the roads with little more than they could carry.
text.effect: Lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A trade caravan offers exotic wares... for a price.
text.effect: You may immediately buy or sell 1 Resource at Market value.

text.flavor: While hunting with falcons, your scout discovers a fertile valley teeming with game.
text.effect:
Place 1 Food token on this Terrain tile.

When Harvesting this Terrain, collect the normal 1 Food Resource from the supply plus the Food token from this tile.

text.flavor: Brigands ambush your Host from the tree line where the path narrows, leaving no easy way to turn aside before steel is drawn.
text.effect: Fight at least 1 round of Combat against Infantry equal to Game Year + 1. If you win, gain 2 Coin. If you disengage after the first round, lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Massive herds of bison or cattle move across the plains, drawing the attention of local nomads.
text.effect: Gain 1 Food.

text.flavor: The year’s wheat crops suffer from a sudden blight, and a portion of your harvest is lost.
text.effect:
Place a Depleted token on this Terrain tile.

Instead of receiving Food during the next Harvest, remove the Depleted token instead.

text.flavor: Unclaimed lands hold roaming herds of hardy horses.
text.effect:
For each Exploring Infantry, roll 1d6.

For each pair of doubles, you may convert 1 Infantry Unit to a Cavalry Unit.

text.flavor: Nomadic herders traverse the plains, offering to trade or seek refuge for the winter.
text.effect: Roll 1d6. On 5–6, gain 1 Levy to your Host, subject to Army limits.

text.flavor: You brave the icy northern wastes. Rumors speak of a people who fish through the ice and never sleep during summer.
text.effect: Roll a D6. On a roll of 1, lose 1 Unit.

text.flavor: A strong wind blows across the region, bringing illness from neighboring lands. Some of your men are already showing signs.
text.effect:
Disease spreads to your units.

For each different Unit type present in your Host, roll a D6.

On a result of 1–2, lose 1 Unit of that type.

Roll separately for Levy, Archer, Infantry, and Cavalry.

Priest is immune.

text.flavor: You find an ancient cobblestone road. Pilgrims once walked this path to sacred lands.
text.effect:
Roll a D6.

  • 1–3: Nothing comes of it.
  • 4: Gain 1 Leadership.
  • 5: Gain 1 Morale.
  • 6: Gain 1 Research.

text.flavor: Bandits haunt the roadside here, striking where the path narrows and the march cannot easily turn aside before steel is drawn.
text.effect:
Roll a D6.

On a result of 5–6 you are able to negotiate safe passage, otherwise lose 2 Coins.

text.flavor: Strange mushrooms and fungi are growing in abundance in a particular area. Some appear to be poisonous, others edible.
text.effect:
You may elect 1 Exploring Unit to sample the fungi. If you do, roll a D6.

On a result of 1 the Unit is killed, otherwise gain 1 Food.

text.flavor: A lightning strike causes a wildfire to spread rapidly across the forest, threatening all in its path.
text.effect:
Place a Depleted token on this Terrain tile.

Instead of receiving Wood during the next Harvest, remove the Depleted token instead.

text.flavor: You encounter a group of skilled woodworkers who offer their services in exchange for protection or a share of profits.
text.effect: Gain 1 Wood. You may spend 1 Coin to gain 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: Your scouts uncover a long-forgotten trail through the trees. It leads to an abandoned, though well preserved settlement.
text.effect: When you reveal the new Clearing, if it does not have a Barbarian Icon gain 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: Your explorers find deep shafts and rusted tools in a mountain cave. Whispers echo in the dark...
text.effect: You may search: Roll a D6. On a roll of 6 the mine collapses and you lose 1 Infantry from your Host (if able), otherwise collect the result in Coin.

text.flavor: Your scouts are lured into the highlands... Where tribal warriors strike from the rocks.
text.effect:
Choose 1:

  • Defend in Combat: Combat vs [Game Year] Infantry Units.
  • Flee: Roll a D6. On a result of 5-6 you negotiate safe passage, otherwise lose 1 Infantry or 1 Morale

text.flavor: A sudden avalanche triggers a landslide, blocking the mountain pass and burying your supply caravan.
text.effect:
Roll 2D6.

For each 1–2, lose 1 Exploring Unit (your choice).

text.flavor: A secluded monastery offers access to rare texts, but their scribes require something in return.
text.effect:
Roll the Resource Vulnerability die.

You may spend 1 Resource of the rolled type to gain 1 Research token.

This roll does not adjust the Market value of this Resource.

text.flavor: The remains of a caravan lie scattered. Clues suggest ambush or betrayal.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Coin.

You may advance 1 Time to honor the dead. If you do, gain 1 additional Coin and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Wild boars are reported in the area, and a hunting party is eager to track them down.
text.effect:
Roll a D6.

Collect 1 Food on a result of 5-6.

text.flavor: Your host comes across a peculiar scene: a seemingly ad-hoc gathering of tribes in heated debate over food, labor, rites, and tolls. Every answer seems to please some while offending others.
text.effect:
Choose 1: Apply the combined Rapport DRM from all tribes. Critical Results apply.

  • Hear Petitions (6+)
    Pass: Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Broker Terms (7+)
    Pass: Gain 3 Coins
  • Exploit the Discord (8+)
    Pass: Gain 6 Coins.
    Fail: Lose 1 Rapport with all Tribes. Tribes not yet encountered are immediately set to Hostile. Do not apply the Global Shortfall Rule. Combat does not occur. Proceed to Arrival.

text.flavor: Your scouts reach a high rise where open ground and distant roads can both be watched. From here, signs of what lies ahead are easier to read than from the march below.
text.effect:
Choose 1:

  • Mark the Clear Road: Gain the Clear Road token.

    When an Explore event triggers, before resolving any part of it, you may discard this token to ignore that event.

  • Scout the Approach
    The next time you reveal a Clearing, if it has a Barbarian Icon, gain 1 Leadership. Otherwise, gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A lone rider wearing silken robes seeks audience, offering trade maps and strange philosophies.
text.effect: May immediately pay 3 Coins for 1 Research token.

text.flavor: Sealed chests contain scrolls of a defunct knightly order. Their oaths and tactics live on in ink.
text.effect: Roll a D6. On a result of 5–6, gain 1 Research. Otherwise, gain 1 Coin.

text.flavor: A mystic woman lives atop the cliffs, visited by nobles and warlords alike. Her prophecies are both respected and feared.
text.effect: You may spend 1 Leadership to gain 1 Research.

text.flavor: Crates of untaxed wine, fine cloth, and carefully wrapped bows lie hidden in a cave. Someone did not want them found.
text.effect:
Roll a D6.

  • 1–4: Collect that amount in Coin.
  • 5–6: Gain the Longbows Advancement. If you already have the Longbows Advancement, collect 1 Research token instead.

text.flavor: Hundreds died here. Bones litter the fields. Your men feel uneasy.
text.effect:
You may assign an Infantry to dig up ancient weapons. If you do, roll a D6.

On a result of 4-6, you gain either Halberds or Longbows (take the card from the Combat Advancement deck and reshuffle it).

Otherwise, the assigned Infantry dies.

text.flavor: A sunken field, filled with bones and discarded charms. The plague visited here once...
text.effect:
May search. If you do, roll a D6.

On a 5–6 you discover new Armor technology. Gain 1 Armor Advancement.

On a result of 1, an illness overtakes your host. Lose D3 units of your choice from your host.

text.flavor: A company of battle-worn knights seeks shelter. They claim to be the last of their order.
text.effect:
May immediately Recruit up to 2 Cavalry, paying 2 Coins for each.

Mercenaries:
  • May exceed Host MU limits
  • Use white Mercenary tokens.
  • Disband from your Host in the Winter season.

text.flavor: The Host finds the aftermath of slaughter: blood in the mud, broken doors, and spoils left among the dead. No one claims responsibility. Your soldiers understand the lesson.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Take What Remains: Gain 3 Coin and 1 Leadership. Gain the Reign in Blood token. Seed one random RB Echo.
  • Bury the Dead: Advance 1 Time and Seed one random BD Echo.

Reign in Blood effect: While this token is active, your Host may not Disengage from Combat.

text.flavor: A ring of painted stones waits in a forest clearing, arranged around a crude image of Middelalderen. The marks look Quietus: part prayer, part boundary, part warning.
text.effect:
If The Quietus have not been encountered, discard this Card with no effect.

If The Quietus have been encountered, refer to your current Rapport with them:
  • Allied: Seed Echo S1.
  • Friendly: Seed Echo S2.
  • Neutral: Seed S3.
  • Hostile: Seed S4.

text.flavor: Brigands step from the roadside and demand coin for safe passage.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
Pay the Toll: Spend 2 Coin.
Refuse: Seed 1 random BG Echo.

text.flavor: Outlaws watch from the trees, laughing as they name their price.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
Pay the Toll: Spend 3 Coin.
Refuse: Seed 1 random BG Echo.

text.flavor: The pass is held by hard men with blades drawn and no patience for bargaining.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
Pay the Toll: Spend 4 Coin.
Refuse: Seed 1 random BG Echo.

ARRIVAL-003.title: Toll at the Broken Causeway (1R)
ARRIVAL-003.setup: A stone crossing has been chained and audited. Nightstone wardens claim the road by right of maintenance and demand recognition before any host passes.
ARRIVAL-003.effect:
Choose 1:
Negotiate the Toll (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership, or gain 1 Rapport and lose 1 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Recognize the Claim (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Food, Wood, or Stone.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Force Passage (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-005.title: Stone for the Dead (1F)
ARRIVAL-005.setup: A burial road has collapsed into a quarry trench. Nightstone masons and mourners alike demand the passage be made right before any host crosses further. They can be bargained with, worked with, exploited, or defied, but not ignored lightly.
ARRIVAL-005.effect:
Choose 1:
Join the Work — Pay 1 Wood: (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Rapport and 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: No additional effect.

Hire the Masons (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Stone and 1 Leadership, or gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Press Them Aside (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-008.title: The Broken Ledger (1W)
ARRIVAL-008.setup: A tally-house has been split open by looters, and Nightstone clerks accuse every traveler of theft until someone pays for order to be restored.
ARRIVAL-008.effect:
Choose 1:
Audit the Losses (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Leadership.

Settle the Claim (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research or 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Call Their Bluff (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-013.title: The Weighbridge at Blackwater (1F)
ARRIVAL-013.setup: A timber weighbridge spans a black-water crossing, its planks marked with old iron measures. Nightstone wardens claim every wagon must be weighed before passage, and every shortage paid in coin, stone, or obedience.
ARRIVAL-013.effect:
Choose 1:
Challenge the Assessment (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 2 Coin.

Assist the Weighmen (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Stone and 1 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Wood.

Falsify the Weight (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 3 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin and Damage 1 space in your Baggage Train.

ARRIVAL-014.title: The Debt Stone (1F)
ARRIVAL-014.setup: A waist-high stone beside the road is carved with debts owed by travelers, lords, and broken hosts. Nightstone collectors claim your march inherits an old obligation from the road itself.
ARRIVAL-014.effect:
Choose 1:
Bargain Down the Debt (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Rapport, but lose 1 Morale.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Question the Debt (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research or 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Extort the Collectors (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 3 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-001.title: The Sealed Archive (1F)
ARRIVAL-001.setup: Ash-grey scribes bar the way before a ruined record-house, disputing whether your march is worthy of entry. The archive may yield guidance or preserved knowledge depending on how you handle them.
ARRIVAL-001.effect:
Choose 1:
Seek Guidance (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership, or gain 1 Rapport and lose 1 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Leadership.

Preserve the Record (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research and 1 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Break the Seal (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-006.title: Ashes on the Guideposts (2C)
ARRIVAL-006.setup: Someone has blackened the route markers ahead and stripped the old way-signs of their script. A small Pale Hands escort claims they can still guide worthy travelers, but not for free, and not for the faithless.
ARRIVAL-006.effect:
If Allied: Gain 1 Leadership.

Choose 1:
Restore the Marks (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Leadership.

Hire a Guide — Pay 1 Coin: (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Rapport and 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: No additional effect.

Take the Hidden Route (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Food and 2 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

ARRIVAL-011.title: Writ of Passage (1S)
ARRIVAL-011.setup: At a collapsed gatehouse, Pale Hands wardens still keep fragments of old authority. They say the road may be taken by force, but legitimacy must be earned.
ARRIVAL-011.effect:
Choose 1:
Present Credentials (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Leadership.

Purchase a Writ (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research and 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Read the Side Margins (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale. Advance 1 Time.

ARRIVAL-015.title: The Road Index (1W)
ARRIVAL-015.setup: Pale Hands scribes sit beneath a canvas awning, sorting weather-stained tablets into long rows. They claim the road ahead has been catalogued before, but only the worthy may learn what was written.
ARRIVAL-015.effect:
If Allied: Gain 1 Leadership.

Choose 1:
Read the Index (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Leadership.

Preserve the Tablets (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research and 1 Rapport.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Take the Forbidden Entry (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-016.title: The Witness Tree (1F)
ARRIVAL-016.setup: Strips of parchment hang from a dead tree, each bearing a name, accusation, or last confession. Pale Hands witnesses ask your host to hear the claims before passing beneath the branches.
ARRIVAL-016.effect:
Choose 1:
Hear the Claims (8+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

Judge the Accused (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Research and 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Twist the Testimony (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 3 Coin.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-002.title: Last Grain Before Frost (1S)
ARRIVAL-002.setup: A hungry settlement watches your column pass. Their wardens have stores hidden, but not enough for everyone through the season. What you take or give here will be remembered.
ARRIVAL-002.effect:
Choose 1:
Offer Relief — Spend 1 Food before the test (6+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Wood and 1 Morale.
  • Fail: Lose 1 additional Food.

Share the Burden (9+)
  • Pass: Gain 1 Morale and 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Coin.

Take the Stores (7+)
  • Pass: Gain 2 Food.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Rapport.

ARRIVAL-007.title: The Festival of Grain (2C)
ARRIVAL-007.setup: The Sun-Touched celebrate the harvest with music, contests, and tables laden with food. Travelers gather from distant settlements, but not every visitor receives the same welcome.
ARRIVAL-007.effect:
Choose 1:

Attend (8+): Determine current Rapport with the Sun-Touched before rolling. Apply the usual Rapport DRM and optional Leadership.
Allied: Pass: Gain 2 Food, 1 Coin and 1 Morale. Fail: Lose 1 Coin.
Friendly: Pass: Gain 1 Food, 1 Coin and 1 Morale. Fail: Lose 1 Coin.
Neutral: Pass: Gain 1 Food and 1 Coin. Fail: Lose 1 Coin and 1 Morale.
